tutorial.title: Controlling While Loops
tutorial.descriptionContent: Use a while loop to loop through code a certain number of times

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent: Let's dive into controlling the times a while loop repeats its code, like this page that uses a loop to run its code from 1 to 10 times.

lessons.title: While Loops
lessons.interactiveContent:
To control the number of times a while loop repeats, we start with a variable set to a number. We call this variable a counter variable.

Make sure to pick 1.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A counter variable controls how many times a while loop repeats. Start it at the first number to display.

Make sure to pick counter, followed by 1.

lessons.title: While Loops
lessons.interactiveContent:
Then, we use a comparison in the condition to compare the counter variable to a number. In this case, counter < 4.

Make sure to pick counter, followed by <, and finally 4.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A counter variable keeps track of loop repetitions. Here, counter starts at 1 and increases inside the loop.

Compare counter on the left with a number so the loop continues while it is below 4.

Make sure to pick counter, followed by <, and finally 4.

lessons.title: While Loops
lessons.interactiveContent:
Inside the code block, we make the condition return false and stop the loop by incrementing the counter variable. Try it with counter++.

Make sure to type counter++.

lessons.title: Changing the condition
lessons.interactiveContent:
Changing the condition tells the loop when to stop. For example, changing the condition to counter < 10.

Make sure to pick 10.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Changing the condition tells the loop when to stop. Make the console end at 9.

Make sure to pick counter, followed by <, and finally 10.

lessons.title: Changing the counter variable
lessons.interactiveContent:
Changing the counter variable's value changes when the loop starts. Like setting counter to 5.

Make sure to type 5.

lessons.title: Code in the code block
lessons.interactiveContent:
Since the whole code block runs, the order you write code affects what the console displays. Place counter++ first to display 6 through 10.

Make sure to pick counter++;, followed by console.log(counter);.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Code order affects the console. Increase each number before displaying it, from 6 through 10.

Make sure to pick counter++;, followed by console.log(counter);.

lessons.title: Question: Incrementing the counter
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does counter++ do?

It increases counter by one each time the loop runs its code blockIt creates the counter variable

It increases counter by one each time the loop runs its code block.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Why does this loop eventually stop instead of displaying the same number forever?

counter++ increases the value used in the condition.counter++ creates the counter variable.counter++ displays counter in the console.

counter++ increases the value used in the condition.
